lines.text: What if every mammal, bird, fish and reptile vanished, but insects stayed?
No birdsong at dawn. The barn is empty, and the fields are perfectly still.
On day one, breakfast changes. No eggs, no milk, no meat.
Every cow, chicken and pig on the planet is simply gone.

segments.caption: The empty lake
segments.fact: FISH GIVE THEM 20% OF ANIMAL PROTEIN

lines.text: Fishing boats come back with empty nets.
More than three billion people get a fifth of their animal protein from fish. Now there's none.
Spring comes, and the bees are still buzzing, so most crops still get pollinated.
But everything that used to eat insects is gone.

segments.caption: Nobody eats the bugs
segments.fact: INSECTS EATEN BY BIRDS EACH YEAR

lines.text: Birds alone eat around four hundred million tonnes of insects every year.
Without birds, bats, frogs and lizards, insect numbers explode.
Caterpillars strip the orchards, and swarms chew through the crops.
In the US alone, bats save farmers billions of dollars a year in pest control. Now that help is gone.
So farmers fight back with nets and sprays, doing the work that birds did for free.
And forests slowly change, because most tropical trees rely on animals to spread their seeds.
We'd survive, hungrier and itchier, on a planet ruled by insects.
Which animal would you miss the most?
